decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to the left end of the set square, raising while turning the gripper down; right arm stays at origin.
Retry with smaller increments after the initial IK continuity rejection.
Continue raising and pitching the left gripper toward a top-down approach, with open fingers.
Move above the left handle region while continuing the downward approach rotation.
Advance to the set-square end at safe height and continue pitching down.
Orient the open fingers across the narrow width of the set square while remaining above its left end.
Lower gradually while finishing the jaw alignment perpendicular to the tool.
Complete in-plane jaw orientation and descend toward a shallow grasp on the set square, away from all cubes.
Carefully lower open fingers around the set square's left-end width; cubes remain untouched.
Continue the slow final descent; visual fingertip-to-tool clearance is still uncertain.
Close around the set-square end at tabletop height, easing upward slightly to avoid pressing into the table.
Level the retained set square in the table plane before using its long edge to push; maintain closed grasp and tabletop height.
Raise only the set square slightly to check retention and relieve table friction; no contact with cubes.
Return to shallow table contact and test a small forward slide of the tool; visual retention remains uncertain.
Slide the set-square end forward slowly at fixed height and inspect whether the long edge follows.
Bring the left end forward to straighten the set square's long edge before its push reaches the blocks.
Advance the set square gently toward the cube fronts while holding its nearly horizontal orientation.
Correct the rejected tensor. Gently sweep the straightedge forward another 15 mm to settle all three cube faces against it.
Continue the gentle straightedge sweep to square the leftmost cube with the other two; keep cube contact low and planar.
The three cube fronts now appear aligned against the straightedge. Release the set square and begin lifting clear for arm reset.
Retract the open left gripper upward and rearward, unwinding its yaw toward the initial configuration without touching the aligned row.
Continue clear retreat and wrist unwinding along the same elbow-up branch.
Blend the wrist back toward the initial forward-facing orientation while retracting toward the left-arm origin.
Continue smooth rearward reset with the gripper open and the aligned cubes undisturbed.
Approach the original EE position and orientation smoothly, keeping the same arm configuration.
Finish approaching the left origin and correct the small right-arm idle drift; the set square and cubes remain on the table.
